reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The King at the Center of the Cross", "body": "Mario Garza opens the weave by arguing, following Rene Guenon's The Great Triad and The King of the World, that ancient kings understood themselves as the bridge uniting Heaven and Earth, seated at the crossing point of a kingdom quartered into north, south, east and west. He cites John Michell's At the Center of the World for kingdoms literally divided by a north south and an east west road, and reads the Rider Waite Emperor card as a central mountain flanked by two peaks. In his telling the king aspires to be the unmoved mover, still at the axle while the wheel of cycles turns."}, {"title": "Polar Symbolism Came Before Solar", "body": "Garza contends, citing Guenon, that polar symbolism is the older and more primordial layer, that a counterclockwise turn like the stars around the pole star returns to the center while a clockwise turn is solar and expansive, and that the pole star is the axle of the wheel of heaven. Chance Garton offers his own cosmological conjecture, flagged as conjecture, that the Earth grows rather than spinning through a vacuum, and he brings up reported underwater lakes and shores as a possible density boundary, treating the vertical z axis as an axis of density where submersibles bounce off denser water."}, {"title": "Kings, Crosses and the Philology Goggles", "body": "Garton walks through words for king across languages: basileus in Greek, rex and lex in Latin, rey, re, roi, krol, kral, Konig, wang, o and melech. He proposes that R and L interchange, that X trades with S and C, and that a hard aspirate turns the French roi into croix, or cross, noting European rei against Brazilian hey. He links Hebrew cohen with khan, and ras or rosh, meaning head, with rex and the Ethiopian ras, then follows basileus into the basilica, the basil leaf, vassals, the basilisk and the Bank for International Settlements in Basel."}, {"title": "The Sacrificed King and the Crucified Savior", "body": "Garza describes a long pattern of the king who is killed when he stops pulling his weight, with the jester dressed as king and ritually mock killed in springtime, and the wandering prince or Fool arriving from outside to dethrone him, all of which he ties to Aries as cardinal fire and sacrifice. Garton reads Ixion, bound to a fiery wheel, as in his view one of many crucified saviors predating Jesus, quoting the author he cites as Nimrod, and Pindar, on the wheel as a Saint Andrew's cross, and adds Saint Eulalia, martyred on that same X shaped cross in 303 AD."}, {"title": "Losing the Center, and Finding It Again", "body": "Garza argues that what marks a dark age is the loss of the center, that people feel ungrounded because everything now runs on external validation and external solutions, and that the heart, the Rosicrucian rose at the crossing of the cross in Manly P. Hall's illustration, and the Freemasonic compass and square all point back to the same still point. Garton describes his biofield tuning practice, where he finds a client's energetic poles drifted out of alignment with their physical center through habitual thinking. Garza closes by reading the Fool as descending the polar mountain to take another turn of the wheel."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The sedulous loremaster of Symbolic Studies, Mario Garza, returns to Vibe Rant to share some of his ever evolving seasonal researches. Why are classic versions of the Emperor Card in the Tarot depicted as mountains? What does the archaic allegorical archive advise us about the sacred center of our realm and of ourselves? Kings, crosses, rams, and the wisdom of Aries are in the mix for tonight's synchromystic show!
